name: PwC
summary: PwC's interviews usually mix behavioural questions with technical or case questions for the line of service you've applied to: assurance, tax or advisory. For many entry-level roles, candidates commonly report an online assessment first, then live interviews, with a case common for advisory roles. PwC publishes five values, from 'Act with integrity' to 'Reimagine the possible'.
rounds: Online application, with an online assessment for many entry-level roles
Screening call with a recruiter (for some roles)
Competency or behavioural interview on your experience and motivation
Technical or case interview for the line of service (often a case for advisory)
Final conversation with a senior manager, director or partner
looks_for: Curiosity about clients' businesses and how they're changing
Clear, structured reasoning in technical and case questions

questions.text: Tell me about a time you spoke up about something that wasn't right.
covers: What was wrong and how you checked before raising it
Who you spoke to and how you put it
What happened next and what you learnt

questions.text: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate grow or get through a hard patch.
covers: What they were struggling with and how you noticed
What you did, without taking over their work
How things changed for them and the team

questions.text: Describe a time you found a better way of doing something everyone was used to.
covers: The old way and what it cost in time or errors
Your idea, and how you tested it and won people over
The improvement, measured if possible

questions.text: Tell me about a time a group you were part of met a tough deadline. What was your part?
covers: The deadline and what made it tough
Your specific contribution and how you worked with others
The result and what you'd do the same way again

questions.text: A client's costs have risen faster than its revenue for two years. How would you structure the problem?
covers: Clarifying the business, its markets and which costs have grown
Splitting costs into fixed and variable, then by area: people, materials, overheads
The likely drivers, the data you'd check, and practical first steps

questions.text: What's the difference between profit and cash, and why can a profitable company run out of cash?
covers: Profit is recorded when earned; cash moves when customers pay and bills are settled
Working capital: slow-paying customers, high stock, or big investments
A simple example and what a business can do about it

questions.text: How would you test whether a company's expenses are recorded in the right period?
covers: Cut-off testing: invoices and payments either side of the period end
Searching for unrecorded liabilities after the year end
Checking accruals and prepayments for reasonableness

questions.text: A client wants to automate its invoice processing. What would you check before recommending it?
covers: Volumes, how standard the invoices are, and where time and errors go today
Data quality, system links and the controls that must stay in place
Expected savings against cost, risks, and a pilot to prove it

questions.text: What does a cyber security review of a company look at? Name the main areas.
covers: Who has access to what, and how access is granted and removed
How systems are patched, monitored and backed up
How the company would detect and respond to an incident, and how staff are trained

questions.text: Estimate how many laptops are sold in Bengaluru in a year. Talk me through your assumptions.
covers: Splitting buyers into groups such as students, working people and businesses
How many own a laptop and how often they replace it, with round numbers
A final figure and a quick sense check

questions.text: Why PwC, and why this line of service?
covers: What the line of service does and who its clients are
Why it fits your skills and interests, with an example
Something specific about PwC you learnt from its people or work

questions.text: Which of PwC's values matters most to you, and when have you shown it?
covers: One value, named once
A short, specific example of you living it
Why it matters for the work you'd do here

questions.text: What questions do you have for us about the team or the work?
covers: Specific questions on clients, the first year or how people learn on the job
A question that follows from something said in the interview
Nothing you could have found on the careers site in a minute

tips: Prepare a story for each of PwC's five values; behavioural questions often map to them.
For a case, ask what the client wants to achieve, lay out your structure, and end with a recommendation and next steps.
Know the basics of your line of service: accounting and audit for assurance, tax principles for tax, a technology or process area for advisory.
Online assessments are timed; practise similar numerical and reasoning tests beforehand so the format isn't new on the day.
Read one or two recent business stories about the industry you'd like to serve and be ready to say what they mean for clients.

sources.title: PwC's purpose, values and behaviours (pwc.com careers)
